problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(2,0)=0,\,{f}_{x}(2,0)=0,\,{f}_{y}(2,0)=2.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,0),$ estimate the value of $f(2.01,0.02).$

feedback.problem:
Let $f(x,y)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,3)=4,\,{f}_{x}(x,y)=2x+y,\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=x.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,3),$ estimate the value of $f(1.04,3.03).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(1,3)+∇f(1,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩ \\  & ≈f(1,3)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,3),{f}_{y}(1,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩ \\  & ≈4+⟨{f}_{x}(1,3),{f}_{y}(1,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(1,3)$ and ${f}_{y}(1,3)$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,3) & =2(1)+3=5 \\ {f}_{y}(1,3) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)≈4+⟨5,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(1.04,3.03)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.04$ and $y=3.03,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.04,3.03) & ≈4+⟨5,1⟩\cdot ⟨1.04-1,3.03-3⟩ \\  & =4+⟨5,1⟩\cdot ⟨0.04,0.03⟩ \\  & =4+5(0.04)+1(0.03) \\  & =4+0.2+0.03 \\  & =4.23\end{aligned}
$$
